name: Sleepy Hollow Campground
note: Small private campground in the Garrett County forest at 2,740 ft, less than a mile from New Germany State Park and its lake, swimming, fishing and boat rentals. 18 RV sites, nine tent sites and five A-frame cabins; 20/30/50-amp electric and rigs accepted to 36 ft, but NO water or sewer at the sites - there is a water filling station beside the bathhouse and a dump station on site. 2025 season rates: $38/night electric site for tent or RV, $28 primitive tent, $75 small A-frame cabin; nightly and seasonal rates both offered, open roughly March/April to December. Bathhouse with showers, general store selling firewood, wifi, 10% military and first-responder discount; also a Harvest Hosts location. Bookable on Campspot. CAVEAT on the pin: three sources disagree by up to 1.7 km on where this sits (US Census rooftop match on the operator's own published address, RV Life's pin 680 m west, Campspot's coordinates 1.7 km west) and Esri imagery is unbroken canopy at all three, so the coordinate here is the address match rather than a confirmed loop. NOT confused with New Germany State Park Campground (id 63), which is the separate state-run campground next door. RV Life 4.5*/$$ ~$39/night (auto 9/2026). --Claude
inclusion_evidence: Operator site sleepyhollowcampmd.com plus a live Campspot booking listing (fetched 2026-09-15): 18 RV sites with 20/30/50-amp electric taking rigs to 36 ft, $38/night for an electric site, dump station and bathhouse -> a real nightly-bookable drive-in RV campground, distinct from adjacent New Germany State Park. Corroborated by VisitMaryland.org, a Good Sam listing, a Harvest Hosts host page and a Yelp page updated May 2026.

lead.water_body: none on site; New Germany Lake is in the state park under a mile away
lead.note: PIN NEEDS A COORD_FIX IF YOU CAN GET ONE - see the note's caveat; Census rooftop 39.63739,-79.10673 used, RV Life says 39.63805,-79.11457, Campspot says 39.640869,-79.124367, and canopy hides the loop at all three. On water: neither the operator nor Campspot claims any water body at the campground itself, both referring campers to the state park next door, so not waterfront is the expected answer - but confirm against whichever coordinate turns out to be right.
